glossary_gaps.why: The only two places this project has ever spelled a Chestburster rendering are PROJECT.md §7.2.0 point 2 and the wave brief, and both write the model sequence as 卵 → 抱脸虫 → 破胸体 → 成体. Principle I applied, so the set is coherent rather than arbitrary: 「虫」 marks the one arthropod-shaped parasite stage (only Stage II earns it — the Facehugger is literally spider/crustacean-shaped, and 抱脸虫 is owner-pinned), while 「体」 marks the -morph form stages (卵形体 / 破胸体 / 成体). Corerules ch.10 backs the split: the Stage III Imp variant is described as 'a miniature version of its adult form' with 'translucent skin, a carapace and rawboned features' — i.e. a small bipedal Xenomorph, not a worm, so 虫 would mis-describe it. ⚠ COLLIDES with ST-A-CRE.cn.json which used 破胸虫 (13 occurrences + the actor name). Controller must break this; see open_issues #1.

Not one of the six stage names — it is a named variant inside Stage III ('Stage III: Chestburster, Bambi Burster, Imp'), the immature form of a Praetomorph. So it does not take the 「体」 stage suffix and does not disturb the family. 幼 carries 'immature / miniature version of its adult form'; 魔 carries the demonic etymology of Imp and the horror register. Rejected 小鬼 (reads as 'little kid' in Chinese, kills the register). Low confidence — only 1 occurrence in this unit; corerules ch.10 has the full description and should settle it.

glossary_gaps.proposed: 卵化 (the process); 卵形体 for the noun, 异形卵 in running prose
glossary_gaps.why: Only the verbal form appears in my unit ('initiate the ovomorphing process' → 启动卵化的过程). 卵化 = 宿主→卵, deliberately NOT 孵化 (= hatching, 卵→幼体, the opposite direction) — that near-homophone trap is the main reason to pin this term now. ✅ ST-A-CRE.cn.json independently arrived at 卵化 (7 occurrences) and 异形卵 (8), so this half of the family is already cross-unit consistent with no coordination.

Chinese has no natural clipping of 异形, and the English alternates Xenomorph/Xeno inside a single row purely for rhythm. Rendering both as 异形 (glossary_alien.json, settled) loses nothing. Note the project rule held: 异形 = the creature, 外星 = the adjective — 外星 correctly occurs 0 times in this unit.

Result label on EV - Facehugger Attacks 1-2, needed in both the `name` field and the `<strong>` opener. 窸窣 is the rustling-scurry sound word; the row's own gloss is 'It skitters forward, single-minded and horrifyingly spider-like'. Dropped the stray trailing ASCII colon from the `name` field, following the shipped Panic Response Table precedent where 'Keeping Cool.' → 镇定 (trailing punctuation dropped in name fields, kept inside the description's <strong>).

Used in EV - Stalker, Scout and Drone Attacks 4-4 and 6-6, which must agree with each other since 6-6's Headbite is the follow-up threatened in 4-4. 内颚/外颚 is the established Alien-lore pair and stays anatomical rather than inventing a second creature word.

Attack name, cross-referenced by 4-4 ('will use a Headbite attack (#6 below)') and titling 6-6, so it must be one string in both places. Kept as a blunt 2-char verb-object to match the neighbouring 咬喉 (Throat Bite) on the Chestburster table.

open_issues: ⚠ #1 CROSS-UNIT TERM COLLISION, needs a controller ruling before assembly. Chestburster: I wrote 破胸体 (6 occurrences, ST-T-REST.cn.json); the sibling ST-A-CRE.cn.json wrote 破胸虫 (13 occurrences PLUS the actor name '破胸虫（第三阶段异形） EV - Chestburster (Stage III Xenomorph)'). Same creature, two words, and the actor's attack button opens exactly my table — a GM will see both in one click. Case for 破胸体: it is the form written in PROJECT.md §7.2.0 point 2 AND in the wave brief, both as 卵 → 抱脸虫 → 破胸体 → 成体; and corerules ch.10 describes the Stage III Imp as 'a miniature version of its adult form' with 'a carapace and rawboned features', which 虫 mis-describes. Case for 破胸虫: PROJECT.md's rule sentence says 不能一个用「虫」一个用「体」一个用「者」, and 抱脸虫 is the owner-pinned anchor. The rule text and its own worked example contradict each other — that is the real defect, and it should be resolved in RULINGS.json, not by a silent sed. Either way the fix is one term in one file; my side is the cheaper one (6 occurrences, no name field). The rest of the family already agrees across both units with no coordination: 抱脸虫, 异形, 卵化, 异形卵, 成体.

#2 UPSTREAM DEFECT (not fixed, count preserved). EV - Stalker, Scout and Drone Attacks 1-1: the English closes the tag mid-word — 'STRESS LEVEL'. There is no Chinese analogue of a word split at that point, so I wrote 压力等级 and preserved the tag COUNT (2 , 1

) rather than replicating the split as 压力等级. If a gate compares tag positions rather than counts it will flag this row.

#3 UPSTREAM DEFECT (silently repaired in the Chinese). EV - Facehugger Attacks 6-6 has an unclosed parenthesis: '(armor has no effect, except the APEsuit.' — no ')'. A dangling 全角 parenthesis reads as a rendering bug in Chinese, so I closed it: （护甲无效，APEsuit 除外）。 This changes no game content. Flagging because the project's policy elsewhere is to preserve upstream defects rather than fix them.

#4 Deliberate divergence worth a controller glance: the EV - Facehugger Attacks table `description` is a heading that I translated (

抱脸虫攻击

) while the table's own `name` stays 'EV - Facehugger Attacks' in English (T-FROZEN). So the sidebar label and the in-table banner are in different languages. That is what the freeze forces — the name is machinery, the description is prose — but it will look like an oversight to anyone reading the assembled pack.

#5 I added id="facehugger-attacks" to that <h2>, per the brief's heading rule. Note it is belt-and-braces here, not load-bearing: RollTable descriptions never go through JournalEntryPage.buildTOC, and no data-hash="facehugger-attacks" exists anywhere in the starterset (I enumerated all 44 distinct slugs). The corpus currently has 0 explicit heading ids, so if the controller prefers attribute-verbatim headings this is the one place to strip.

#6 APEsuit left in English inside EV - Facehugger Attacks 6-6. It is a gear proper name and it points at the corerules item 'Weyland-Yutani APEsuit' (not in the T-FROZEN item_names register, so a later unit MAY translate it). If the item族 unit renames it, this one prose mention must move in the same commit or the reference goes stale.

#7 The EV - Sub Table Facehugger Attacks description quotes the parent table by its frozen English name — 「“EV - Facehugger Attacks”表中“4 尾部擒抱”一项的子表」— deliberately, so a GM reading it can find that table in the sidebar, where it is also English. If the controller ever unfreezes table names, this string is a hard sync point.
